newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton up on mill buying and quota hopes.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton up on mill buying and quota hopes.

text.p: Cotton prices lifted further on the local market on Tuesday, propelled by fresh mill buying and hopes of higher export quotas, dealers said.

In the spot deals Punjab saw-ginned rose by 20/30 rupees at 1,580/1,700 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while F-414 climbed up by 40/45 rupees to 1,935/1,950 rupees per maund. Bengal-deshi was steady at 900/950 rupees per maund while Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) rose by 600 rupees to 13,300/13,500 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).
"Daily arrivals of new crop cotton are sliding due to end season considerations," one trader said.

"Sentiment at the close was firm amid shortage of good quality cotton," he added. "Fresh mill buying lifted prices recently but looking at the sharp jump in the prices I am expecting mill demand to peter out at the current level."
